title: Orbit search and split search
statement: For a function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ and a Boolean word $w$, searching the indices from $0$ through $|w|$ for the first one at which the acceptance test holds on the corresponding iterate of the split step, starting from the empty word, returns the same result as the least-index search for $i+f(i)=|w|$; both searches return none if no such index exists.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a function from natural numbers to natural numbers
replaced:
For every function $f$ and every word $w$, searching the indices
$0, \dots, \abs{w}$ for the first $i$ at which the width-parametric
acceptance test succeeds on the $i$-th iterate of the split step (the unary
candidate $1^i$) returns exactly the width-parametric split search for $f$
at length $\abs{w}$.
